Meshallem et hakkofer. uchegon shehaya muad lehappil atzmo al bene adam bevorot, vehaidna chaze yarka babbor vehippil atzmo labbor leechol yarka veharag et haadam, shehashshor patur mimmita hoil veharag shello bechavvana, vehabbealim meshallemin et hakkofer, deitrabbe kofer afillu sheharag shello bechavvana kidamrinan leel:

Rabbi omer vechulei. vahalacha kerabbi. hilkach im hichnis shoro birshut baal habbayit setam velo kibbel alav lishmor, baal habbayit patur, deha lo kibbel aleh netiruta. vehammachnis nammi patur, lefi shehichnis birshut:
Ba acher velibba. nafach baesh veheela shalhevet, kemo belabbat esh (Shemot 3). veit sefarim degarse nibba, miggizrat niv sefatayim (yeshaya 57), kesheadam medabber menaanea bisfatav veruach yotze:
O afar. shellichacha niro venitkalkel:
O derech harabbim. shesh esre amma, kedigle hammidbar:
Rabbi shimon omer hakkol lefi haddeleka. lefi gova haddeleka vegodel shiurah. shekkeshehaesh gedola kofetzet lemerachok. vahalacha kerabbi shimon:
Hamefarek et hammitta lehatebilah. af al pi shemmittaheret keshehi shelema, peamim shehi gedola veenah yechola likkanes bammikve vetzarich lefarkah:

Vehannogea bachavalim. garsinan, kelomar, ben mefarek ben nogea bachavalim tahor. uvemitta shennitmet bemet o vemishkav hazzav ayre, uchegon sheen bammitta arukka ushete cheraayim, vaafillu hachi tzarich lehatebilah, kede shello tachazor letumatah kesheyyechabberenah. vehannogea bachavalim tahor, demikkevan shepperkah shuv en hachavalim chibbur:

Hachevel meematay chibbur. bitchilla kesheadam mesareg et hammitta shelema vesoreg bah shelosha vattim vaadayin nishar hachevel aroch harebe, nitmet hammitta nitma hachevel, vehannogea bachevel, tame, dechullo chibbur hoil vesofo lesargo:
Min hakkesher velifnim. im kashar chevel acher leze hachevel shessoreg bo, en hachevel haacher chibbur min hakkesher velachutz:
Nime hakkesher. keshekkoshrim shene chavalim ze vaze mannichin meat merashe hachavalim mizze umizze yotzim chutz lakkesher, vehen nikraim nime hakkesher:
Hannogea betzarko tame. dechevan detzorech lakkesher hem, sheim haya kosher berosh hachevel mammash haya hakkesher nittar, nimtza sheellu hannimin maamidim hakkesher vechakkesher damu:
Rabbi yehuda omer shalosh etzbaot. havu chibbur, dehu tzorech hakkesher. tefe lo:

Chamishsha devarim chayyavim bachalla. degamrinan challa mippesach, neemar befesach matztzot lechem oni (Devarim 16) veneemar lechem bachalla, vehaya baachalchem millechem haaretz (Bamidbar 15), ma lechem haamur befesach davar habba lide chimmutz, af lechem haamur bachalla davar habba lide chimmutz. veen lecha ba lide chimmutz ella ellu chameshet hamminim bilvad:

Umitztarfin ze im ze. lehashelim shiur haissa hachayyevet bachalla. velo sheyyitztarfu chullan yachad, demin besheeno mino eno mitztaref, keditnan lekamman resh perek 4, ella hachittim mitztarfim im hakkussemin bilvad mippene shehem minan, vehasseorim mitztarfim im hakkol chutz min hachittin, veaf al gav dechussemin min chittin hem, lav min chittin davka ella min seorim veaf min chittim, umitztarfin im hachittim vehasseorim. uvayrushalmi mashma deim nilloshu yachad mitztarfin afillu min besheeno mino, aval im lo nilloshu yachad ella sheachar kach hayu nogin haissot zo vazo, min bemino mitztarfin, shello vemino en mitztarfin:
Vaasurim bechadash. kedichtiv (Vayikra 23) velechem vekali vecharmel lo tochlu ad etzem hayyom hazze, vegamrinan lechem lechem mippesach:

Umilliktzor millifne happesach. sheasur liktzor meechad mechameshet hamminim kodem ketzirat haomer, dichtiv baomer (Vayikra 23) reshit ketzirchem, shettehe techilla lechol hanniktzarim, veatya reshit reshit mechalla, ketiv hatam (Bamidbar 15) reshit arisotechem, uchetiv hacha reshit ketzirchem, ma lehallan mechameshet hamminim af kan mechameshet hamminim:
Veim hishrishu. echad mechameshet hamminin hallalu, kodem ketzirat haomer:
Haomer mattiran. umuttar lekatzro achar ketzirat haomer, dichtiv (Shemot 23) asher tizra bassade, mishshaa shennizra venishrash bassade:
Veim lav. shello hishrishu ella achar ketzirat haomer:
Asurim ad sheyyavo omer habba. shel shana habbaa:
Makkel. shel etz bealma sheasao vet yad lakkurdom lefi shaa, shello kevao vetocho:

Chibbur lattuma bishat melacha. deaf al gav divappe nafsheh peshute chele etz lo mekabbele tuma, hacha vet yad hu, veyadot nitrabbu lechol torat tumat hakkeli o haochel, veim nitma hakkurdom nitma habbet yad, vechen im naga tuma babbet yad nitma hu venitma hakkurdom immo. vedavka vishat melacha have chibbur lattuma, shello vishat melacha lo, deshello vishat melacha adam asuy lezarko leven haetzim:

Deyusetar. keli hameshammesh lishne tzedadim. deyu, shenayim. setar, tzad. kedimtargeminan listar chad. vehu makkel sheyyesh bo shene nekavim echad millematta veechad millemala, ushete yetedot techuvot bahen achat mimmizrach lemaarav veachat mitztzafon ledarom, vehannashim mesechot bo et hammatve shebbappelech, vekorin lo 191 belaaz. ufeamim sheosin otan yadot mibbarzel umekabbelin tuma:
Kevao vichlonas. kava haddeyusetar dehaynu hammakkel im shete yetedotav bichlonas, dehaynu etz aroch vegadol hattakua baaretz:

Tame. haddeyusetar mikkan vaelach im naga vo tuma, dahave hammakkel chibbur laytedot ben bishat melacha ben shello vishat melacha, kevan shennikba, sheen adam asuy lezarko leven haetzim. aval hakkelonas atzmo eno chibbur lo, sheim naga tuma vakkelonas lo nitma haddeyusetar:
Asa vo haddeyusetar. shekkava shete hayetedot begufo shel kelonas:
En tame. min hakkelonas ella ma shehu letzorech hayetedot lehasech et hammatve, vehashshear ben millemala ben millematta tahor, shehakkelonas aroch hu vegadol:
Kisse. shehu asuy, ukevao vichlonas, hakkisse tame midras, veen hakkelonas chibbur lo lihyot mittamme midras kemoto:
Asa vo chisse. min hakkelonas atzmo asa chisse:
En tame ella mekomo. dehaynu tzorech hayeshiva. ushear hakkelonas tahor:

Kava hakkisse vekorat bet habbad. sheotzrim bah hashshemen min hazzetim. hakkisse tame midras, vehakkora enah chibbur utehora. veim meetz hakkora atzmah hakkisse asuy beroshah haechad, af hakkisse tahor, deomrim lo amod venaase melachtenu. vetanya vetorat kohanim, asher yeshev alav yitma, yachol afillu yeshev al haeven veal hakkora, talmud lomar, keli, velo even velo kora. otzi et ellu, velo otzi chele avanim kele gelalim kele adama, talmud lomar hakkeli, keli hameyuchad lekabbel tuma, vechelim hallalu en mekabbelim tuma leolam. en li ella chisse vesafsal vekattedra hameyuchadim lishiva, minnayin tevat habballanim, teva sheppitchah mitztziddah, areva mishshene log ad tisha kabbin shennisdeka veeno yachol lirchotz bah raglo achat, talmud lomar vechol hakkeli, ribba. yachol afillu chafa sea veyashav aleha, tarkav veyashav alav, talmud lomar asher yeshev, hameyuchad lishiva, lo sheomrim lo amod venaase melachtenu:
Echad shor veechad kol behema linfilat habbor. dichtiv (Shemot 21) kesef yashiv livalav, lechol mide deit leh bealim:
Ulehafrashat har sinay. dichtiv (sham 19) im behema im ish lo yichye, vechayya bichlal behema. im, lerabbot et haofot:
Uletashlume chefel. dichtiv (sham 22) al kol devar pesha, kol mide devar peshia hu:
Velahashavat aveda. lechol avedat achicha (Devarim 22):

Lifrika. azov taazov immo (Shemot 23). af al gav dichtiv (sham) chamor sonaacha, kol behema bichlal, deyalfinan chamor chamor mishshabbat shenneemar bo (Devarim 5) shorcha vachamorcha vechol behemtecha:
Lachasima. lo tachsom shor bedisho (sham 25), yalfinan shor shor mishshabbat:

Lechilayim. deharbaa, af al gav dichtiv (Vayikra 19) behemtecha lo tarbia kilayim, have nammi chayya vaof bichlal, deyalfinan behema behema mishshabbat. vechen leinyan kilayim dehanhaga delo tacharosh beshor uvachamor yachdav (Devarim 22) yalfinan shor shor mishshabbat, dehu haddin lechol shene minim shel behema chayya vaof. umihu leinyan pesak hahalacha min hattora eno chayyav ella keshechoresh umanhig bishne minim sheechad tame veechad tahor, dumeya deshor vachamor, ella sheasru chachamim kol shene minim, ben sheshshenehem temeim ben sheshshenehem tehorim:
Uleshabbat. dichtiv shorcha vachamorcha vechol behemtecha, vechayya bichlal behema. vechol, ribbuya hu, lerabbot ofot:
Sheddibber hakkatuv bahove. bedavar haragil lihyot:
Orez. lav min dagan hu, vechol sheeno min dagan patur min hachalla, veen adam yotze vo yede chovato befesach:
Im yesh bah taam dagan chayyav bachalla. veaf al gav deen baddagan keshiur challa:
Perot chutza laaretz shennichnesu laeretz chayyavin bachalla. dichtiv (Bamidbar 15) el haaretz asher ani mevi etchem shamma, shamma attem chayyavim ben beferot haaretz ben beferot chutza laaretz:
Mikkan lesham. meeretz yisrael lechutz laaretz:

Rabbi eliezer mechayyev. dichtiv (Bamidbar 15) vehaya veachlechem millechem haaretz, ben sheattem ochlim oto baaretz ben sheattem ochlim oto bechutz laaretz, hoil velechem haaretz hu, chayyav bachalla:
Verabbi akiva poter. deshamma mashma leh miuta, shamma attem chayyavim, veen attem chayyavim bechutza laaretz, af al pi sheattem ochlim millechem haaretz. vahalacha kerabbi akiva:
Nittelet min hattahor al hattame. velo chayshinan shemma yiggeu ze vaze:
Notel kede challa. shiur challa shetztzarich littol min hattahor vehattame, notel meotah issa hattehora shello hurema challatah:

Venoten pachot mikkabbetza baemtza. ben hattemea vehattehora, defachot mikkabbetza eno metamme, umanniach hachalla al oto pachot mikkabbetza hamechabber ben hattemea vehattehora, sheen hachalla mekabbelet tuma bechach:
Kede sheyyittol min hammukkaf. shettihye hattemea mechubberet lattehora al yede oto pachot mikkabbetza, ucheillu hattemea utehora issa achat:
Vachachamim osrin. littol min hattehora al hattemea, dechayshinan shemma yigga zo vazo, ella notel min hattahor leatzmo umin hattame leatzmo. vahalacha kachachamim:
Ad sheyyekatztzea. sheyyachtechenna vitakkenenna lishiva. vahalacha kachachamim:

Af al pi shekkevaah bakkotel temea. tumat met o sheretz. velo vatla mittorat keli velo amrinan keli hamechubbar lakkarka kekarka dame ella cheshehaya mechubbar lakkarka mittechillato, o shennaasa chede leshammesh et hakkarka:
Uferagin. korin lo baaravi 641, uvelaaz 373:

Ufachot mechameshet revaim battevua. tevua sheosa pachot mechameshet revaim kemach chayyav bammaasrot, vehaissa shennillosha min hakkemach hahu petura min hachalla, lefi sheshshiur haissa lehitchayyev bachalla hi chameshet revaim kemach veod, kelomar meat yoter mechameshet revaim:
Hassufganim. lechem shebbelilato rakka veasuy kisfog. perush acher rekikim dakkim, targum urekike matztzot, veispogin:
Hadduvshanim. metugganim bidvash, i nammi nilloshim bidvash:
Haiskeritin. targum tzappichit, iskeriton. uvelilatan rakka meod:
Vechallat hammasret. challa chaluta bammachavat, targum machavat, masrita:
Hamedumma. sea shel teruma shennafla lefachot mimmea sein shel chullin, venaasu chullan medumma vaasurim lezarim, ufatur min hachalla, dichtiv (Bamidbar 15) tarimu teruma, velo shekkevar nitrema:
Hammizran. kemin ezor o avnet shel arig shekkorchim oto seviv hammitta kede lechabber perakeha. ufeamim shehu gadol harebe venigrar veyotze chutz min hammitta:
Hayyotze min hammitta. vehammitta temea midras:
Kol shehu. afillu yotze kamma ammot chutz lammitta, hakkol tame:
Rabbi yose omer ad asara tefachim. tame vetumat hammitta. measara ulemala tahor. vahalacha kerabbi yose:
Sheyare mizran. mizran shebbala venikra, kamma yishtayyer mimmennu veyihye tame:
Shiva tefachim. divtzir mehachi lo chazi lemidi vela chashiv keli:

Chevek. yesh mefarshim, beged av vekashe shemmesimim al hachamor keshebba min hadderech vehu mazzia, kede shello yitztannen leachar shemmesirin mimmennu haukkaf. veyesh mefarshim, shemmesimim oto al masseoy hachamor kede shello yufsad im yerdu alav geshamim:
Hatturemel. kis gadol shel or sheharoe noten chafatzav letocho, uvetoch hatturemel yesh kisin ketannim kemo hammegurot batteva:
Hachemet. nod shel or:
Shehabbetzim shellah mekabbelot immah. keshemmafshitin orot haelim vehatteyashim hazzecharim nishar haor shebbimkom habbetzim kemin kis katan, veim nifchatu tehorot, devatal bet kibbul shellahen:
Echad meesrim vearbaa. lefi shebbaal habbayit issato meuta, uvefachot meechad meesrim vearbaa en bah kede mattana, vehattora amra tittenu, sheyyehe vo chede netina:
Vehaose lemishte veno. af al pi sheose issa merubba lo pelug beissat baal habbayit:
Nachtom haose limkor bashshuk. issato merubba, uveechad mearbaim ushemona yesh bah kede mattana:
Vechen haishsha haosa limkor. af al pi sheissatah meuta lo pelug befat heasuy limkor:
Nitmet. hoil velisrefa omedet, echad mearbaim ushemona:
Chayyavin alehen mita. zar haochlan mezid chayyav mita bide shamayim, dechalla ikkarya teruma, uvitruma ketiv (Vayikra 22) umetu vo ki yechalleluhu:
Vechomesh. haochlan shogeg meshallem keren labbealim, vechomesh lechol kohen sheyyirtze:

Vaasurim lezarim. bechinnam hi shenuya, dechevan shechayyavim hazzarim alehem mita vechomesh peshita daasurim lezarim. ulerabbi yochanan deamar chatzi shiur middeorayta, matzinan lememar ditna asurim lezarim lachatzi shiur sheen bo lo mita velo chomesh, aval issura deorayta miha ikka:
Vehen nichse chohen. sheyyachol lemachran velikkach bahen avadim vekarkaot uvehema temea:
Veolin beechad umea. im nitarvu bemea shel chullin:
Uteunim rechitzat yadayim. habba ligga bahen tzarich littol yadav techilla, shessetam yadayim poslot et hatteruma, veet hachalla, sheaf hi nikret teruma:
Vehaarev shemesh. tame shettaval eno ochel batteruma ad sheyyaariv shimsho, kedichtiv (Vayikra 22) uva hashshemesh vetaher veachar yochal min hakkadashim, vehu haddin lechalla:

Veenan nittalim min hattahor al hattame. gezera shemma yitrom shello min hammukkaf, mishshum demistefe shemma yigga hattame battahor vitammeennu, vaanan bainan shehattorem yitrom min hammukkaf keditnan besamuch:
Veen nittalin ella min hammukkaf. garsinan, uferush mukkaf karov vesamuch:
Min haddavar haggamur. shennigmera melachtan, vechalla mishshettitgalgel haissa:
Ad sheyyeshayyer miktzat. dechalla uteruma ketiv behu reshit, uvainan sheyyehu sheyarehen nikkarim:
Veshor eno meshallem ella nezek. dichtiv (Vayikra 24) ish baamito, velo shor baamito:
Ufatur middeme veladot. dichtiv (Shemot 21) ki yinnatzu anashim, anashim velo shevarim:
Veim huzzeka vahem baal happerot chayyav. vehane mille shehuchleka venichshela bahen. aval im achla mehen ad shemmeta, baal happerot patur, dahava la shello tochal:
Katrav. meforash lemala perek kele mattachot, shehen shene etzim mishshene tzidde haol vehen nekuvim, umachnisim betoch oto nekev etz ushemo katrav, vekoshrim oto shello yishamtu habbakar:
Baayin. beged shel tzemer o or o sak shekkorchim al tzavvar habbehema, vehaol alav:
Avot. etz aroch veav shebbammachresha, shennichnas betoch haol:
Vehacherev. etz asuy kidmut cherev shettofes bo hachoresh:
Vehakkorech. etz akom dome lemerkav, vehu hannatush al hakkarka beet hacharisha:
Bayyatzul. etz shettofes oto hachoresh beyado, uvo matte hammachresha lechol tzad sheyyirtze. uferush yatzul, matte. lo tatte mishpat (Devarim 16), metargeminan lo tatzle din:
Ayin shel mattechet. tabbaat shel mattechet:
Lechayayim. shene etzim shebbenikve haol:

Arayin. asuy kemin keli shel mesattet avanim uvo meshabber gushim shel afar. vekaruy arayin milleshon arer titarar (yirmeya na), aru aru ad hayesod bah (tehillim 137) veen halacha kerabbi yehuda shemmetaher ballechayayim:
Hachovel. vechamma hu yafe. sheim haya tzarich haya mocher atzmo beeved ivri, veze shehizziko hifsido mamon ze:
Kayyotze vaze. lefi ma shehu meunnag rav tzaaro ucheevo:
Tzemachin. avabuot levanot:

Shevet. kol yeme hacholi roin oto keillu hu shomer kishshuin venoten sechiruto shel kol yom, shehare en rauy limlacha acheret afillu belo choli, shehare nikta yado veraglo vehu kevar natan lo demehen:
Hakkol lefi hamevayyesh. adam kal shebbiyyesh bashto merubba:

Vehammitbayyesh. lefi chashivuto bashto merubba. vechullehu chamishsha devarim mikkera nafke. nezek, dichtiv (Shemot 21) ayin tachat ayin, veen lomar ayin mammash, dichtiv (Bamidbar la) velo tikkechu kofer lenefesh rotzeach, lenefesh rotzeach i atta lokeach kofer aval atta lokeach kofer lerashe evarim, sheim simme et en chavero noten lo deme eno, vehayenu ayin tachat ayin. tzaar, nafka lan mippetza tachat patza (Shemot 21), dikra yetera hu lechayyev al hatztzaar vaafillu bemakom nezek, dela tema hare kana yado veyesh alav lechatchah, ella omrim haya alav lechatchah besam veze chatachah bevarzel vetziaro, lefichach meshallem et hatztzaar. rippuy veshevet, rak shivto yitten verappo yerappe (sham). vedavka keshehacholi ba mechamat makka. aval im pasha hachole beatzmo veavar al divre harofe, shuv en hammazzik chayyav bashshevet verippuy shetztzerichin mechamat peshiuta. boshet, dichtiv (Devarim 25) vekatztzota et kappah, mamon. vedin tora sheen yecholim ladun beshum din shebbaolam ella dayyanim hassemuchim beeretz yisrael, dichtiv (Shemot 22) ad haelohim yavo devar shenehem, veen nikraim elohim ella dayyanim hassemuchim beeretz yisrael. ella shebbehalvaot umikkach umimkar vehakenaot vehodaot uchefirot danin bahem bechutza laaretz keillu hem sheluchim shel bet din shel eretz yisrael ushelichutayhu kaavdinan. veze bilvad bedavar hammatzuy veyesh bo chesron kis, vechen behema shehizzika beshen varegel shehem muadim, o shehizzik adam bivhema. aval behema shehizzika adam, o adam beadam, en danin oto bechutz laaretz kelal, ella menaddin et hachovel o et hammazzik ad sheyyaale im baal dino leeretz yisrael o sheyyitten derech peshara karov lema shennire beene haddayyan, aval davar katzuv en poskim alav. vechen haddin bechol hakkenasot hakketuvot battora uvechullah talmuda, en govin otan dayyane chutza laaretz, ella shemmenaddin mi shennitchayyev bahen kemo shebbearnu:
Venaga bahen hammet. keshehen keruchim yachad:

Temeim tumat shiva. beha lo faleg rabbi yose. dedavka vetumat midras kaamar ad asara tefachim tame measara velachutz tahor, aval lishar tumot, afillu mea amma kullo chibbur. kegon mizran shehu karuch al hammitta venichnesa hammitta leohel hammet o naga vesheretz, vechen im nichnas katze min hammizran leohel hammet o naga besheretz, nitmet hammitta nitma hammizran, nitma hammizran nitmet hammitta, vaafillu haya hammizran yotze min hammitta mea amma:

Pershu temeim tumat shiva. velo havu kechelim shennishtabberu, kevan dechol echad mehen keli bifne atzmo. af al gav dilinyan kabbalat tuma chashuvim kichli echad ucheshennaga tuma veechad mehen nitma haacher:
Shennittelu shete arukkot shellah. velo nishtabberu, vehen reuyot lehacheziran limkoman, hilkach lo tahara hammitta mittumatah bintilat haarukkot:

Nishtabberu chadashot temea. shehare hayeshanot kayyamot velo nishtannu hannekavim, vehave chenitparka evar evar vechol evareha shelemim. aval nishtabberu hayeshanot, tehora, lefi shehayeshanot hen shehayu bammitta cheshennitmet, ucheshennishtabberu have hammitta shever keli, delo chazya velo arukkot:
Ganav al pi shenayim. kelomar shenayim meidin oto shegganav:
Ganav umachar beshabbat. aval tavach shehu anush sekila, kam leh bidrabba minneh:

Vetavach beyom hakkippurim. sheen zedono ella karet. uchegon delo atteru beh velo lake, dekayma lan kol chayyave malkiyyot shoggim chayyavim betashlumin. aval chayyave mitot bet din, afillu shoggim, peturim min hattashlumin:
Vetavach umachar veachar kach met aviv. aval met aviv veachar kach tavach, tana sefa defatur, deshello hu toveach veshello hu mocher, shehare yarash et aviv:
Bishne ellu. bitrefa uvechullin baazara. dekasavar rabbi shimon shechita sheenah reuya lav shemah shechita. aval lirfua velichlavim, shechita reuya hi, dei bae matze achel minna:
Sadin shehu teme midras. sherauy littamme midras kaamar, velo shennitma midras mammash. deim ken addetane sefa aval tame teme met, litne aval tame magga midras, kidtane vehakkometz rabba:
Vaasao vilon. masach lappetach, o vilon lassefina. vedavka sheasa vo shinnuy maase, aval machashava enah motziattu mide tuma shehayu reuyin lah:
Aval tame teme met. mippene shehashshammash mitchammem kenegdo umitattef beshulav lifamim, hilkach lo vatel mittorat keli:
Meematay tohorato. shebbatal torat midras mimmennu:

Mishsheyyittafer. battosefta muchach devet shammay bau sheyyikraennu vitakkenennu lemiddat happetach, veyitpor bo lulaot litloto vemasach o visfina. uvet hillel deamre mishsheyyikkasher, lo vau keria, ella mishsheyyikshor bo hallulaot kede litloto vahem. veit sefarim degarse, bet shammay omrim mishsheyyittaver. vehi hi. kelomar mishsheyyishberuhu veyikrauhu chede letafro lemiddat happetach:
Rabbi akiva omer mishsheyyikkavea. meet sheyyitle oto al happetach o al hassefina. vahalacha kevet hillel:

rashi: Ed beliyyaal yalitz mishpat. yaid leadam melitzat mishpete yissurin umita:
Ufi reshaim yevalla aven. haaven yivlaehu:
targum: Sahada riglaa memayek bedineh ufumehon derashie mappik aata:

rashi: Nachonu lalletzim. hakkadosh baruch hu zimmen lo shefatim shel tzaraat laze halletz hamsapper belashon hara (Bamidbar Rabba 13:4):
targum: Mittaknin limemikne dine umachata legishmehon desichle:

Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:111-122: And Ra'avad explained, in the Gate of Holiness, the matter of "purity brings one to holiness," and began the gate with the verse (Leviticus 20:7), "sanctify yourselves and be holy" - and he said, relevant to our subject, in these words: I shall first explain what the two holinesses mentioned in this verse are; and likewise what they said in the beraita of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, "purity brings one to holiness" - I shall explain what purity is and what holiness is, and from this you will know what the two holinesses are.

And he says first, that impurities are of two kinds: those found by touch, and those not by touch. By touch - such as touching carcasses and their being moved, touching creeping things, the lying and sitting [defilement] of a zav, a zavah, and a leper, the sighting of a seminal emission, and the impurity of the dead. And likewise one who transgresses sins, such as one who has relations with forbidden relatives, and one who eats forbidden things - these are impurities that are by touch, for one who has relations with forbidden relatives and one who eats forbidden things is called impure, as it is written in the passage of forbidden relations (Leviticus 18:24), "do not defile yourselves with any of these," and "and you shall be defiled by them" (ibid. 11:43). And the impurity that is not by touch - such as the seeing of the eyes, the hearing of the ears, and the utterance of the lips, in a matter that is not fitting to see, nor to hear, nor to speak of - and the contemplation of the heart in matters that are forbidden.

Purity too is found by touch and not by touch. For the purification of touchings and movings, and of seminal emission, and of plagues, and of the impurity of the dead, is through immersions and sprinklings, and other matters explained concerning the leper - and this is purity by touch. And the purity that is not by touch is separation from sin and forbidden things, and the cleanliness of the heart, the thought, and the tongue, and the closing of the eyes and the stopping of the ears from seeing and hearing evil - all these are called pure, as it is written (Leviticus 16:30), "from all your sins before the LORD you shall be pure," and it is written (Ezekiel 36:25), "from all your impurities and from all your idols I will purify you," and it is written (Isaiah 33:15), "and shuts his eyes from seeing evil," and so on, and it is written (Proverbs 22:11), "he who loves purity of heart, for the grace of his lips the king shall be his friend," and it is written (Psalms 24:4), "clean hands and a pure heart" - and if he is careful of these he is called pure, and whoever is not careful is called impure; and one who speaks things unfitting for him is called impure of lips, and one careful of this is called pure of lips.

It follows that impurity is of two kinds and purity of two kinds - except that there is a distinction between separating from the impurity of sins and forbidden things and separating from other impurities. For one who separates from touchings and other similar impurities is called only "pure," as it is written (Leviticus 14:8), "and he shall wash in water, and be pure." But one who separates from sins and forbidden things is called both pure and holy - pure, as we have said, and holy, as it is written in the passage of forbidden relations (Leviticus 20:7), "sanctify yourselves and be holy," and also in the passage of creeping things it is written (ibid. 11:44), "sanctify yourselves and be holy." And not only that, but the other impurities do not involve the impurity of thought, but with the impurity of sins and forbidden things, just as one must separate from the sinful act itself, so must he separate from thinking of it, that he not contemplate the sin in his heart - and if a thought about them comes to him, he must force himself and remove it from his heart, all the more so that he not intend to complete it in his heart. And since a completed thought is what leads to the deed and is considered as a deed - concerning this it is said (Ezekiel 14:5), "in order to take hold of the house of Israel by their heart" - and this is the second holiness that Scripture warns of: "sanctify yourselves" through deed, "and be holy" through thought. Do you not see what is written at the end of the verse, "for I am holy" - just as I am holy in deed and in thought, so shall you be holy - from this you learn that a person is not called holy until he is sanctified in deed and in thought.

And now you shall understand and know that a person cannot attain this attribute until he sets aside, of what is permitted to him, some portion, and fences himself with a fence around things that are permitted, which are the way and path that lead to habituating oneself in sin - along the lines of what they said (Niddah 13b), whoever puts his hand below his navel, his hand should be cut off; and as they said (ibid.), whoever holds his member and urinates is as though he brought a flood upon the world; and as Rabbi Yosi said (Shabbat 118b), I have never in my life gazed at my own circumcised member - and they asked, if so, why did they call him "our holy Rabbi"? They answered, he had an extra measure of holiness in that he never put his hand beneath his belt. And all this separation was a fence, so that the desire of forbidden relations not attach to him - for the evil inclination quarrels with a person and accuses him, to entice and seduce him, and this is its way: it entices him to sate his soul and fulfill all his desires with everything permitted to him; and after it has taught him to fulfill all his desires with the hunger of his soul, when his hand does not find what is permitted to him, it will entice him to fulfill his desires from the forbidden, easily - and from the light [prohibition] to the severe, and from the severe to one more severe still, until it says to him, go and worship idols and deny Him who spoke and the world came into being, that there is no judgment and no judge, no Garden of Eden and no Gehinnom and no other world. And so the wise man said in the book of Ecclesiastes (cf. Ecclesiastes 9:3), "this is an evil among all that is done under the sun," and so on, "for the living know that they shall die," and so on, "go, eat your bread with joy," and so on, "enjoy life with the wife whom you love," and so on - all these are the words of the evil inclination - to this point, relevant here.

We shall not elaborate further on the explanation of the verse as he, of blessed memory, explained it, so as not to lengthen; and he said afterward: and therefore one must strengthen and fortify himself and stand firm to fight his desires, so that he have a virtue in his soul over the soul of the beast, which has no restraint from whatever it can attain for its desire - for the desire that overpowers a person is from the power of the vegetative soul, which is the animal [soul], and therefore the wicked, who follow after their desires, are likened to beasts, as Scripture says (cf. Psalms 49:13), "man in his glory abides not," and so on, and the wise man said (Ecclesiastes 3:21), "who knows the spirit of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the beast, whether it goes downward to the earth" - "the spirit of man" refers to the soul of the righteous, which ascends upward, and "the spirit of the beast that goes downward" refers to the soul of the wicked, who are likened to a beast.

And the meaning of these words is this: he said, above this (verse 20), "all go to one place; all were from the dust, and all return to the dust," and so on - meaning, there is no difference in death between the righteous and the wicked, nor even between man and beast, for all shall die and return to the dust, and among all the living there is none who can discern any distinction between one and another - and "who knows" concerning the level of the souls, whether the soul of a righteous man ascends upward and the soul of a wicked man descends downward to the earth - meaning, below the earth, which is the depths of Sheol - among all the living there is none who can discern that distinction, except the Creator alone. And this matter is known through wisdom to the wise, the masters of contemplation, but there is no known proof of it from the matter of life and death, for all are equal in this - and therefore he says "who knows," meaning, who can discern their level? For were the distinction demonstrable, the wise and the foolish alike would know it - but there is no sign or proof of it in life and in death.

And behold, though all souls are equal, in their death they return to the place of their desire and their striving in their lifetime - for the soul of the righteous, taken from the place of intellect, and which held fast to its intellect and its [proper] desire, returns in its death to the place of its source; but the soul of the wicked, which desired the vanities and pleasures of the world, and did not remember its origin from before, returns likewise to the place of its desire - to this point, relevant here.

And at the conclusion of the gate, he explained briefly the discourse we are explaining, and he said, of blessed memory: "watchfulness" is when a person is careful and guards himself before the deed comes into his hand. And "alacrity" is at the time of the deed, that he perform his commandment with alacrity, not out of laziness, and if a sin comes into his hand, he flees and separates from it with alacrity. "Cleanliness" is the cleanliness of his body and his garments from soiling, along the lines of what they said (Shabbat 114a), any Torah scholar found with a grease stain on his flesh is liable to death. "Purity" comes with regard to impurities, that he guard himself from impurities, and if he touches them, he purifies himself and eats his non-sacred food in purity. "Holiness" is the holiness of the heart and thought, as we have said. "Piety" is one who acts beyond the letter of the law in every matter, called a chassid - and all these he explains their reasoning from the verses in Shekalim - to this point.

According to our approach, let us return to explain the matter of "purity brings one to holiness," and the rest of the discourse - and although above we did not explain anything concerning "separation" [perishut], because we said it is included in holiness, nevertheless, according to the wording of our version, it is fitting to explain something about it. And the matter is that holiness includes two things, as we elaborated in the Gate of Holiness: the one, "turn from evil," and the second, "and do good" - and according to our version, we say that "separation" is from the aspect of "turn from evil," and "holiness" is "do good." But according to the Yerushalmi, which does not have the reading "separation," both aspects are included in holiness, as explained there.

And the intent of saying "purity brings one to holiness" is this: the essence of purity is the purification of each and every limb from blemish - such as the purification of the tongue from slander and other blemishing things, and the purification of the eyes from gazing at forbidden relations, and similarly for the other limbs. But holiness is a further, more inward, fence - for besides not speaking slander, he abounds in silence; and the holiness of the eye is that he not gaze beyond four cubits - as we elaborated in the Gate of Holiness concerning the holiness of each and every limb.

And Ra'avad, peace be upon him, explained, in the Gate of Holiness, the matter of "holiness brings one to humility" - the matter being that when a person attains the aforementioned holiness, humility necessarily follows from it - and the reason is that the essence of holiness is a person's separation from the affairs of the world, in order to cleave to his Creator, as He says (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I, the LORD your God, am holy" - and we elaborated in the Gate of Holiness on the explanation of this verse - see there. And since a person is cleaved to his Owner, humility necessarily follows upon him, for if they revile and disgrace him, he will not regard this world enough to respond to his disgrace, for what they say about him is a disgrace of this world, and all of it pertains to the body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:123-135: And even if they revile him in a matter touching a blemish of the soul, the soul, being holy, does not regard the disgrace done to it, for it considers this an atonement for its iniquity, and all is a cause from Him, blessed be He, to atone for its iniquity - as King David, peace be upon him, said (2 Samuel 16:10), "the LORD has said to him, curse." And further, if they disgrace it, its Master, to whom it is attached, will regard it - and so King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 38:15), "and I was as a man who does not hear, and in whose mouth are no arguments; for in You, O LORD, do I hope; You will answer, O LORD my God." And further, a servant who stands before his master - if a man comes and disgraces him before the king, it is a disgrace for the servant to respond before his master - and for these two reasons King David, peace be upon him, said "for in You, O LORD, do I hope." And to this second reason may be attributed precisely "for in You, O LORD, do I hope" - like a servant sitting before his master who waits for his master to respond to his insult. And to the first reason it may be attributed that he said "You will answer, O LORD my God" - since You are my God, to whom my soul is cleaved, and You are my God, it is fitting for You to regard its insult.

It is also possible [to understand] the attribute of humility along the lines of the attribute of humility of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him - for when Miriam and Aaron spoke about him, it is written there (Numbers 12:3), "and the man Moses was very humble." And there is an allusion to the reason for his humility in the Tikkunim (page 5b): because of the abundance of his cleaving to the Creator, he was ashamed to separate from Him and to respond, and the Name responded on his behalf. And along this path too it is possible to say that King David, peace be upon him, said, "You will answer, O LORD my God."

Also, the attribute of humility follows for a person through his contemplating the greatness of the Creator, which has no end or limit - as Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said (Exodus 16:7), "and what are we?" - for we are not within the bounds of a creature compared to His greatness, may He be exalted - as we shall elaborate on this in the Gate of Humility, with God's help.

And this is the inward fear explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 2 - to fear His greatness. And this fear is attained only through holiness, as it is written (Psalms 34:10), "fear the LORD, His holy ones" - for if one follows the desires of the world, he has no fear at all.

And it follows that all the levels mentioned to attain holiness are all aspects of fear, and holiness is included among them, and fear is bound to humility. And so are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Tikkunei Zohar 5b), "and humility is bound to fear," this is what is written (Proverbs 22:4), "the reward of humility is the fear of the LORD" - and we copied this discourse in the Gate of Fear, chapter 3.

It follows that saying "holiness brings one to humility" is the matter of "fear brings one to humility" - and this is when a person considers, when they revile him and say everything to him, that he is not important as a creature, for one does not respond except one who considers himself something, and says, "shall one like me be reviled?" But one who considers that he is not a [significant] creature, along the lines of "and what are we?" which Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said, certainly will not respond. And further, he should consider that what is said about him is true, that it is a deficiency in the creation and existence of the world, from the side of his iniquities, such that it would have been better for him not to have been created - and he should not regard himself as having the standing of a creature, and will not come to respond at all.

And a person acquires all this attribute of humility now through acquiring holiness - for whoever walks after the stubbornness of his heart in the desires of this world thinks that the whole world is his, and none acquires the attribute of humility except one who is stripped of the affairs of matter and physicality, as explained; for the arrogant one, the world does not suffice for the height of his heart. But the discerning one, when he contemplates that all the goods of this world are a passing shadow and a withering flower, that a person himself is here today and tomorrow in the grave, and that there is no reality of a dwelling for the soul in this world at all, but everything is to prepare him for his eternal home - he separates from the desires of this world and draws upon himself holiness, in order to cleave to his Creator, who is the true purpose, for whose reward the soul waits, to shine in the light of life.

Like the parable of a person whose eyes are open, who sees the sweetness of light, and at some time it happens that he becomes blind - that person waits forever for when the veil of blindness will be removed from his eyes through good ointments, so that he may return to seeing the bright light. So the soul, hewn from the light of the supernal life in the supernal world, when the Holy One, blessed be He, imprisons it in this turbid body, the sight of the supernal lights becomes sealed from it - and the discerning person takes for himself the ointment of the holiness of Torah and commandments, and through this his soul is sanctified and cleaves to the bright light, which is the light of Torah, called "light," as it is written (Proverbs 6:23), "and Torah is light" - and he repents, to remove the partition separating between him and his God. And even though he will suffer - for even the blind man suffers when his eyes are treated, whether with a strong salve or something else, and nevertheless he endures it in order to see the light, and sometimes he suffers over the doubt whether it will help or not - but one who suffers through repentance certainly benefits by removing the blindness of his soul, through which it cleaves to the Creator, and through this the veil of matter is removed from it; for even though it remains clothed in matter, the light of the soul will increase over the body, and the body will not be a veil separating between it and its God - and this is the acquisition of the attributes stated in this discourse, up to the attribute of holiness, which is to remove the veil separating from the soul until it cleaves to the Creator. And the other attributes mentioned - humility, fear, and piety - are all links of one chain that unfold from holiness, for holiness is their father, and humility and the rest are its offspring; for just as one has holiness, humility must necessarily follow, as explained. And with all this, one must give a connection and relation between humility and fear of sin.

And when the reader considers what was explained in the Gate of Holiness concerning the holiness of each and every limb, he will see that humility must necessarily follow holiness, and they are one bond, brothers who will not be separated - for if he sanctifies his eyes as stated there, he thereby has lowered eyes, which is one of the conditions of humility. And if he sanctifies his tongue as stated there, certainly he will not utter insults from his mouth as one who is angry does. And if he sanctifies his heart, he must distance from it envy and hatred - behold, he is humble. It follows that all the conditions of humility and its particulars depend on a person's sanctifying himself properly, as we explained there.

Further, it is possible to give another connection and relation of holiness to humility, and through it may be understood the reason and connection of humility to fear of sin. And the matter is that the essence of holiness depends on the holiness of thought, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayetze, page 155a), whose words we copied in the Gate of Holiness - that concerning the holiness of thought it is said (Leviticus 20:7), "sanctify yourselves and be holy" - and it is impossible for the holiness of thought to come except through the soul, as we elaborated in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 4.

And in the Zohar (Parashat Tetzaveh, page 182a), in the explanation of the verse (Isaiah 2:22), "cease from man, whose breath [neshamah] is in his nostrils" - he said there that when a person is angry, the soul departs from him - and not specifically the neshamah, but even the nefesh, as it is written (Job 18:4), "he tears his soul [nafsho] in his anger." And through this may be understood the precision of his wording there, where he says, "and he has the holy spirit [ru'ach] within him, which comprises three," as we have established that there is nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah. And he further says on: for these three powers are all one. And this whole introduction is to reconcile the verses, since one verse says "he tears his soul [nefesh] in his anger," and one verse says "whose breath [neshamah] is in his nostrils" - and for this he preceded and said that all three are one bond, and all of them depart, and the blemish is in all of them.

And so he further says on: and not only that, but the supernal holiness is uprooted from its place, and a strange god settles in its place. It appears that the whole reality of holiness, from nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah, all departs, and a strange god rests there. And he further says: whoever converses with him is as one who has literally joined himself to idolatry - and if some ru'ach or nefesh had remained, it would not be literal idolatry, for there would still be some holiness in him; rather, certainly all of it departs.

And we are compelled to say that this blemish that reaches the nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah are not the nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah of Atzilut, but the nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah from the aspect of Chayah and Yechidah [or: from the mode of the Chariot and the Throne] - which the blemish blemishes, for the intent is not merely departure, but that they are actually blemished, as they said, of blessed memory: and if he brings that holy soul into another service, this defiles it, and it departs from the service of its Master. And he further says on, that this holy soul is torn and defiled because of his anger, and so on. But concerning the soul of Atzilut, we cannot speak of impurity and blemish, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 98b), in these words: there is an Adam who is an angel, and this is Metatron; and there is an Adam in the image of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is His Atzilut, and this is yud-heh-vav-heh, alef-dalet-nun-yud - and he has no Beriah, Yetzirah, or Asiyah, only Atzilut, and in this place there is no sin and no death - this is what is written (Psalms 5:5), "evil shall not sojourn with You" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:136-147: And if a blemish is found in one who has a soul of Atzilut, it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 124a) that the intent is not an actual blemish, that would darken its light, but rather the departure of the soul of Atzilut is the "blemish" that reaches it - and we copied this discourse in the Gate of Fear, chapter 9 - see there.

And behold, based on these introductions from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, we can say that what the discourse says, "holiness brings one to humility," is this: whoever merits the soul of Atzilut, who is certainly holy, as we copied the discourse of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 4, will merit humility, so that he not come to anger in a way that would blemish the soul - for that supernal holy soul will not be given to one who blemishes it, at every time it departs from him; for the angry person, having that evil attribute, becomes angry over a trivial thing. Rather, certainly, once he has already merited the soul of Atzilut, which is holy, it will bring him to humility, so that his inclination is subdued in such a way that holiness not be lost from him, and it shall be fulfilled in him (Proverbs 12:28), "no harm shall befall the righteous." And one who has not merited the holy soul, in whom the external force still has some grip, will also be brought to anger, so that a strange god rest in him, because he has not been purified from his iniquities as is fitting. Therefore he must strive to attain the attribute of humility through all the aforementioned attributes, until he attains holiness - and since he is holy and the external impurity has no part in him, certainly it will not defile him through anger, which defiles him from within and from without, as explained there in Parashat Tetzaveh.

And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, because of the merit of his supernal soul, had great humility - "and the man Moses was very humble, more than any man," and so on (Numbers 12:3) - and yet, nevertheless, it is said of him (Numbers 31:14), "and Moses was angry," and so on, and they explained, of blessed memory (Vayikra Rabbah 13:1), that a halachah was hidden from him - for according to the subtlety and merit of the soul, a small thing will blemish it.

And along these lines we shall understand his saying, "humility brings one to fear of sin" - for "fear of sin" means that he fears lest even a small sin come into his hand, for according to how much he has merited a supernal soul, so must he fear sin. And the parable for this is the stain of oil that falls on garments - for a stain falling on a linen garment is not equal to a stain falling on a fine woolen garment, nor to one falling on garments of silk and embroidery. So the reality of the blemish is not equal for one who has a nefesh, one who has a ru'ach, and one who has a neshamah - and this is what they explained, of blessed memory (Yevamot 121b), on "and all around Him it storms mightily" (Psalms 50:3) - the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with the righteous to a hairsbreadth, for a hairsbreadth is a great blemish according to the subtlety of their soul, like a great iniquity is to the rest of the people, [as heavy as] the rope of a wagon.

And it is possible that this is why Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai trembled at the hour of his death (Berachot 28b), saying, "I do not know by which path they are leading me" - for according to his wisdom, he certainly merited a supernal soul, and a small blemish would be considered great.

And whoever merits humility will merit fear of sin, and it follows of itself - for just as he guards himself from anger so that his soul not depart from him, and cause "one sinner to destroy much good" (Ecclesiastes 9:18) - for they said in Parashat Tetzaveh that after a person sins through anger, would that he be resanctified, because a strange god rests in his body and does not depart easily - therefore he shall fear sin, from blemishing again, even a small sin, so as not to lose the virtue of his soul; for sometimes the blemish will be such that the holy spiritual soul departs and does not return again, and it is a loss that does not come back, and it will require many preparations until it returns to how it was - would that it return.

And according to the ways I explained above concerning "holiness brings one to humility," by these same ways the matter of fear of sin will also be settled - for the one who sins literally before the king is not comparable to one who is in his courtyard, or one who is in his province; so too, one who draws near to the Holy One, blessed be He, through his good deeds, and thinks that he stands before Him always, and because of this has humility, as explained - for this same reason he will fear sin, even a small sin, for he will be ashamed to sin before the King before whom he stands, for it is not fitting to provoke the King in any small or great matter.

"Fear of sin brings one to..." and so on. All that we intended to explain in this beraita is to explain the attribute of piety [chassidut], for it is the acquisition of the attribute of love, as it is written (Psalms 31:24), "love the LORD, all His pious ones" - for whoever reaches the level called "chassid" is a lover, and the holy spirit rests upon him.

And behold, the attribute of piety, in general, is to conduct himself in all his affairs beyond the letter of the law, as they say in the Gemara (cf. Yerushalmi, chapter 8, halachah 4): "is this not the teaching of the pious - one must act beyond the letter of the law"? And this attribute is one of His attributes, blessed be He, through which He conducts Himself with His creatures, as it is written (Micah 7:18), "for He delights in kindness [chesed]," and likewise (Exodus 34:7), "keeping kindness for thousands," and "abundant in kindness" (ibid. 34:6), and many similar verses.

And after a person is complete in fear, so that he does not sin even a small sin, he transcends the attribute of judgment and the attribute of kindness rests upon him. And the reason is that when a person sins even a little, the attribute of judgment necessarily must be with him to purify and chastise him for that blemish, and when the judgment against him is complete, then kindness receives him - and this is the reason Michael brings near the souls of the righteous (Zohar, Parashat Lech Lecha, page 80a; Tosafot Menachot 110a), for the right is what brings near after the souls have been purified from the River of Fire (Zohar, Parashat Pekudei, page 211a).

And behold, the attribute of Chesed has branches, and whoever wishes to merit it must hold fast to its branches, and the branches of Chesed are explained in Scripture. The first attribute one must hold from Chesed is the Torah, which flows from it, as it is said (Proverbs 31:26), "and the Torah of kindness is on her tongue," and as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Avot, chapter 2, mishnah 5), "nor is an ignorant person [am ha'aretz] pious" - and he explained, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Tzav, page 33a), a sweet matter concerning this: he said that the Torah flows from Chochmah, which is the yud, and the chassid is called "chesed" when he brings the yud, which is Chochmah, into it - namely, "chesed-yud" - and the ignorant person, who has not merited Torah, has not merited Chochmah, and therefore it is not fitting for him to be called "chassid," for he lacks the yud.

And further, in order to merit this, one must occupy himself with Torah from midnight onward until the light of morning, in order to receive the thread of kindness that flows from Chesed upon the Shechinah, and upon those occupied in Torah who have taken hold of her - as they elaborated in the Zohar in several places, and especially in Parashat Vayikra (21b) - and this is what they said, of blessed memory (Chagigah 12b): whoever occupies himself with Torah at night, a thread of kindness is drawn upon him by day - and "night" is called [in this context] after midnight, for before midnight it is called "eve," as they explained in the Tikkunim (page 20).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:148-160: Further, among the attributes of Chesed is to hold fast to charity and acts of kindness in all their particulars, as will be explained in its place, with God's help - for all these are branches of Chesed.

Further, one must fast if he has the strength, as they said in Ta'anit (11a-b): if he can afflict himself, he is called holy; and if not, he is called a sinner. And if he can afflict himself, he is called holy and pious, for it is written (Proverbs 11:17), "a man of kindness rewards his own soul." And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Ta'anit, ibid.), in these words: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said, whoever sits in a fast is called pious, as it is said, "a man of kindness rewards his own soul." And Rashi, peace be upon him, explained "rewards his own soul" as one who separates his soul from food and drink, as in "on the day Isaac was weaned" [gomel]," from my teacher's mouth. Alternatively, "gomel" is a term for reward, meaning he completes his soul for his Owner.

And the reason he is called "a man of kindness" may be said based on what they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Shemot, page 20b), that it is like the image of the rose, which is red and white, and when it is pressed by fire, everything turns white, for the water that comes out is white. So too one who sits in a fast and diminishes his fat and blood, and the fire prevails over him - the fragrance rising from his mouth is like the fragrance of the sacrifice that was reduced through fire and turned white, and he is atoned for. It follows from this that he is called by [the attribute of] Chesed, which is whiteness.

And certainly the words of Reish Lakish are said only of one who has sinned and needs to repent - for if he fasts, he is called "a man of kindness." And the reason is that since he sinned through the sustenance that flowed to him from the side of Chesed, he must reward his soul from sustenance, eating and drinking, and thereby he pays it reward measure for measure - "with what it sinned, it shall be punished," for a person sins only through eating and drinking, as explained in the Gate of Holiness. But a Torah scholar who has not sinned need not fast - and the proof is from Hillel the Elder, as we shall copy shortly - for because he was pious, in that he never in his life grew angry, he would eat as an act of kindness to his soul.

And further, Reish Lakish himself said there that a Torah scholar is not permitted to fast, in these words: Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba said in the name of Reish Lakish, a Torah scholar is not permitted to sit in a fast, because it diminishes the work of Heaven - to this point. And Rashi, peace be upon him, explained "it diminishes the work of Heaven" - he becomes weak and cannot study.

And in our time, no Torah scholar is free of sin, especially from slander or the other categories that do not receive the presence of the Shechinah, and therefore it is fitting that he fast. And should you say that Torah atones for sin, I answer you from King David, peace be upon him, who was a Torah scholar, head of the Sanhedrin, and nevertheless all his days were in fasting after he sinned, as we shall explain in the Gate of Repentance (chapter 3).

And further, it is possible to give another reason why one who fasts is fittingly called "chassid": because one who eats is sustained according to the nature of the world, like the other creatures that eat to sustain their bodies, and the world was created according to nature, which is "Elohim" - for "ha-teva" [nature] equals in numerical value "Elohim" - and therefore the world was created with Elohim, "in the beginning God [Elohim] created" (Genesis 1:1), and the name "Elohim" is mentioned there thirty-two times, and all things that follow nature - such as oil that ignites and water that extinguishes fire - this is according to nature. And behold, the pious one reverses nature and says, "He who said to the oil that it should burn, can say to vinegar that it should burn" (Ta'anit 25a). And along these lines, one who fasts, not wishing to conduct himself according to nature like the other creatures, certainly his sustenance is according to Chesed, which is a subtle, spiritual sustenance - and this is along the lines of the sustenance of Torah scholars, whose sustenance is the sustenance of the soul, flowing from Chochmah, as explained in the Gate of Holiness. And therefore it is fitting that he be called "chassid" - "chesed-yud" - for the yud partners with Chesed to sustain the pious who hold fast to the Name.

And so you will find that the angels are sustained from the side of Chesed, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayera, page 104a). And therefore souls in the World to Come are sustained from the side of Chesed, for the soul is called "the daughter of a priest," as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, pages 95a-b), for it is written (Leviticus 22:12), "and if a priest's daughter marry a stranger, she may not eat of the offering of the holy things" - implying that if she did not marry a stranger, who is the evil inclination, she eats of the offering of the holy things flowing from Chesed, for all holiness is from the side of the right, the yud; and so "she shall eat of her father's bread" indicates this - and so in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 166b), concerning "to cause those who love Me to inherit substance" - see there. And a sign for this matter (Psalms 62:13), "and to You, O LORD, belongs kindness, for You render to a man," and so on.

And in any case, if he needs to eat, or to bathe himself in a bathhouse for the health of his body, he is also called "a man of kindness rewards his own soul" - like the deed of Hillel the Elder, peace be upon him, brought in Vayikra Rabbah (34:3) on the verse "and if your brother becomes poor" (Leviticus 25:39), in these words: "a man of kindness rewards his own soul" (Proverbs 11:17) - this is Hillel the Elder, who, when he took leave of his students, would walk along with them. They said to him, where are you going? He said to them, to perform a commandment. They said to him, what commandment does Hillel perform? He said to them, to bathe in the bathhouse. They said to him, is this a commandment? He said to them, yes - for if the statues of kings, which are set up in circuses and theaters, the one appointed over them scrubs and washes them, and they raise for him wages - and not only that, but he is elevated among the ranks of the kingdom - how much more so we, who were created in [God's] image and likeness, as it is written (Genesis 9:6), "for in the image of God He made man." And so Hillel the Elder would say to his students, at the hour he took leave of them: I am going to perform an act of kindness with this guest [ushpiza] who is in my house. They said to him, do you have a guest every day? He said to them, this wretched soul - is it not a guest within the body? For today it is here, and tomorrow it is not here. Another interpretation: "a man of kindness rewards his own soul" - one who distributes charities. "And he who troubles his own flesh is cruel" - Rabbi Alexandri said, this is one to whom joy comes and he does not draw his relatives to him because of their poverty - therefore Moses warns Israel, "you shall surely give to him" - to this point. And "one who distributes charities" - he gives charity, and this is proven in Vayikra Rabbah.

Further, one who holds fast to the attribute of Chesed is one who hears his own disgrace and is silent, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Yalkut Tehillim, remez 669), on the verse (Psalms 16:10), "You will not give Your pious one to see corruption" - in these words: the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "chassid," as it is said (Jeremiah 3:12), "for I am pious [chassid], says the LORD" - and David called himself "chassid," as it is said (Psalms 86:2), "preserve my soul, for I am pious"; "You will not give Your pious one to see corruption" - Rav Huna said in the name of Rabbi Alexandri: whoever hears his own curse and is silent is called "chassid" - and David heard his curse and was silent.

And this attribute is one of the attributes of the lover, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded (Shabbat 88b) on the verse (Judges 5:31), "and those who love Him shall be like the sun going forth in its strength" - our Rabbis taught: those who are insulted but do not insult, who hear their disgrace and do not respond, who act out of love and rejoice in suffering - of them Scripture says, "and those who love Him shall be like the sun going forth in its strength" - to this point.

And so among the attributes of Chesed is that he not bear a grudge nor take vengeance nor grow angry - for so the prophet Jeremiah said (Jeremiah 3:12), "return, backsliding Israel, says the LORD; I will not cause My anger to fall upon you, for I am pious, says the LORD; I will not bear a grudge forever."

And the general rule is that since a person transcends the attributes of judgment and cruelty and deals with his fellow creatures beyond the letter of the law, he merits the attribute of Chesed - for by strict law, if he rests without ill will, it would be fitting for him to respond to his disgrace and to be angry with one who has blemished his honor; but one who forgives merits Chesed, just as the Holy One, blessed be He, deals with His creatures in the attribute of Chesed, as it is said (Psalms 103:10), "He has not dealt with us according to our sins."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:86-98: However, he should liken himself to his Creator by gazing upon everything of holiness - for just as His providence, blessed be He, is to flow to the holy, as it is written (Psalms 33:18), "behold, the eye of the LORD is upon those who fear Him" - and through this he causes the eye of Arich Anpin to shine into the eyes of Ze'ir [Anpin]. And it appears good to intend this when gazing upon something of holiness, and he will merit in the future that "eye to eye they shall see, when the LORD returns to Zion" (Isaiah 52:8) - and so they said there (Zohar, Parashat Naso, page 130a), and the righteous, the supernal meritorious ones, are destined to see with wisdom - this is what is written, "for eye to eye they shall see" - when? "when the LORD returns to Zion" - and it is written (Numbers 14:14), "that You, LORD, are seen eye to eye" - to this point. And without doubt none merit this level except the righteous who guarded their eyes properly, as they said, "the righteous, the supernal meritorious ones."

Further, we find in "purity" a great matter relevant to practice, namely what they explained, of blessed memory (Yoma 72b), on the verse (Psalms 19:10), "the fear of the LORD is pure" - in these words: Rabbi Yochanan said, this refers to one who studies Torah in purity. What is that? He marries a wife and afterward studies Torah - to this point. And without doubt, in order for a person to attain the cleaving of his thought to his God, he must first marry a wife, and through this his thoughts will be purified - for without a wife it is impossible for him to attain any completeness, since he is lacking and blemished, a possessor of a defect; certainly, when he is married he is a complete person, as it is said (Genesis 5:2), "male and female He created them, and called their name Adam" - as they elaborated in Parashat Vayikra (7b).

Further, purity is found concerning the table: "upon the pure table" (2 Chronicles 13:11). And although this concerns the matter of law, that it is called "pure," as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Chagigah 26b), nevertheless the Torah is expounded in several ways, and we can say that "pure" is written to teach a person moral discipline, that his table be pure - meaning, that he not be drawn after bodily pleasures that come from the side of the evil inclination, for a person's table is called an altar, to atone for him - and when he is not drawn after the pleasures of his inclination, certainly through this he subdues his inclination, and it becomes an altar of atonement to purify his iniquities.

Further, purity is found concerning the heart, "create in me a pure heart, O God" (Psalms 51:12) - and this is the essential point relevant to our subject of cleaving: for if the heart is pure, all the limbs are pure, as they explained, of blessed memory, in Midrash Shocher Tov (Midrash Tehillim, Psalm 14 [sic]), in these words: "I, the LORD, search the heart, I test the kidneys" (Jeremiah 17:10) - why does He mention the heart and the kidneys more than all the other limbs? Rather, the eyes follow the heart, and the 248 limbs follow the heart, and since the kidneys give counsel and the heart decides, therefore He mentions only these, and the Holy One, blessed be He, examines them. And so it says (1 Chronicles 28:9), "and you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve Him, for the LORD searches all hearts" - these are the two hearts, the good inclination and the evil inclination. A parable of an architect who built the city with rooms, sewers, and caves; after some time he became a tax collector, and the people of the city began hiding from him inside the rooms and the caves. He said to them, fools, why do you hide? Am I not the one who built this city? I am the one who built the caves and the rooms! So too (Isaiah 29:15), "woe to those who go deep to hide their counsel from the LORD" - to this point.

And in the Gate of Fear, chapter 7, we copied a similar parable - however, that parable was said concerning one who transgresses in secret, whereas here it is expounded concerning one who thinks thoughts in his heart, as it says, "woe to those who go deep to hide their counsel from the LORD" - and the rooms and caves mentioned in the discourse are the chambers of the heart and the kidneys.

And when a person contemplates this matter, his thought is purified - for the Name created him, and created his heart and his kidneys, and He knows his hidden depths, and before Him all is revealed, darkness like light, and he stands before Him always - and how could he not be ashamed to think a thing not according to His will?

And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, further explained in Bereshit Rabbah on the verse (Jeremiah 32:19), "great in counsel," and so on, in these words: "great" - "behold, You have made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and Your outstretched arm; nothing is too wonderful for You" (ibid. 32:17). Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah: what is "behold, You have made the heavens and the earth"? From that time, nothing is too wonderful for You. Rabbi Chagai in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak (1 Chronicles 28:9): "and you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve Him with a whole heart and a willing soul, for the LORD searches all hearts and understands every imagination of the thoughts" - even before the thought is completed in a person's heart, it is already revealed before Him. Rabbi Yudan in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak said: even before a creature is formed, its thought is already revealed before Him. Rabbi Yudan said of himself (Psalms 139:4), "for there is not a word on my tongue, but, lo, O LORD, You know it altogether" - even before my tongue is engaged, lo, O LORD, You know it all - to this point. And behold, from the plain sense of his words there is proof for our intent, without our elaborating on it.

And when a person contemplates that the Shechinah is above his head, it is fitting that he purify his brain and his heart, so that the Shechinah find a place in which to rest - for these are the two primary limbs of a person, in which the essence of vitality depends, and therefore he must purify them from every blemish that blemishes them, for a small thing will blemish them because of their extreme subtlety and spirituality, since they allude to a supernal place in Atzilut, as explained in the Tikkunim (Introduction, page 17a).

And corresponding to the purity of thought, King David, peace be upon him, said elsewhere (Psalms 24:4), "clean hands and a pure heart." I have already explained "clean hands" above, and copied the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, concerning cleanliness. And afterward he says "and a pure heart" - in this manner, that he not draw his will and his heart to the Other Side, but rather draw them after the service of the Holy One, blessed be He. "Who has not lifted up his soul to vanity" - "nafsho" [his soul] is written but read "nafshi" [my soul] - and they have already established: "nafshi" is the soul of David, the side of faith; "nafsho" is literally a person's own soul - because when his soul departs this world, it ascends through the worthy deeds it performed in the world, to go among all those [worthy ones], along the lines of (Psalms 116:9), "I shall walk before the LORD in the lands of the living" - and because he did not lift up his soul to vanity, "he shall receive blessing from the LORD," and so on - to this point. Behold, it is explained in this discourse the virtue of one who repairs his deeds and his thoughts for the service of his Owner, because his soul is part of the Shechinah - this is "nafsho" and "nafshi," and all is one - and according to the repair of his soul, he repairs above, and therefore he will merit what King David, peace be upon him, said, "I shall walk before the LORD in the lands of the living," and "he shall receive blessing from the LORD," namely the Shechinah, as is known.

And from the affirmative you infer the negative: one who lifts up his soul to vanity and defiles his thought blemishes, Heaven forfend, above, and his soul shall not ascend to the mountain of the LORD nor to His holy place.

And behold, one must purify the heart from envy, hatred, rivalry, and all the evil attributes that depend on the heart, such as worry, sighing, sadness, anger, mockery, and the like - and when the heart is empty of all this, it is a fitting dwelling for the Shechinah, as explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 6, page 22b), that a person must repair a fitting dwelling for the Shechinah in his heart, namely through the repair explained.

And further they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 29, end of page 72), that a person's inside must match his outside. He said there that the wine, which is the Torah, must be guarded and sealed in a good jar, and he said the jar is the heart - and if this jar has been poured with the wine of the evil inclination, it needs rinsing three times, and needs rinsing and washing like the cup of blessing, meaning that his inside matches his outside; and in these words: and when this jar, which is a pure heart within and without, [is fit], wisdom dwells there, of which it is said (Proverbs 8:22), "the LORD possessed me [kanani] at the beginning of His way" - "kanani" is certainly "kankan" [jar]; and if this jar is pure, it is said of it, "and be innocent" [ve-nakeh]; and if not, "whoever touches it shall not go unpunished [lo yinakeh]" (ibid. 6:29) - to this point.

And so too the matter of the purity of thought: for the brain is an important vessel, more subtle than the heart, and therefore it is in the head; and you know, concerning tefillin, that one does not lower [an object] from greater holiness to lesser holiness - namely, [one does not take] the strap of the head-tefillin to make it into that of the hand-tefillin, even though the passages written in the head are the same as those in the hand - rather, since they were placed in the head, they acquired greater virtue and spirituality, and one must not lower them to make them into the hand-tefillin. Therefore one must purify his thought all the more.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:99-110: And whoever merits to purify his thought will merit, in the future, what they said, of blessed memory (Berachot 17a): the righteous sit with their crowns upon their heads. And they merit the crown upon the head only because they purified the brain in their heads, so that the Shechinah would crown herself upon them - and in the future too they merit this.

And it appears that the secret of "their crowns upon their heads" is what is said of Joshua the High Priest (Zechariah 3:5), "and they set a pure mitre upon his head" - and it says "a pure mitre" because the crown was made for him not merely [as an ordinary crown], but because he purified his thought, as explained. And it is possible to say - and this appears to be the essential meaning - that the pure mitre was made for him from the commandments dependent on the head, such as donning tefillin, the spreading of tzitzit over one's head, and the commandment of the corners of the head [pe'ot]; and likewise the purity of thought through the pure intentions by which a person unifies himself to his Owner.

And concerning the matter of purity, we find in the Zohar and the Ra'aya Meheimna places that differ from one another - in Parashat Korach (page 176a), and also in Parashat Chukat (page 180b), it is explained that the priest is "holy" and the Levite is "pure," and therefore the [red] heifer, which is from the side of the left, comes to purify and not to sanctify, for the essence of purity is on the left. But in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Ekev, page 273b), that purity is on the right and holiness on the left.

And concerning holiness, it will be explained further on, with God's help. However, concerning purity, it appears to me that there are two kinds of purity: the first is purity through water, as explained above, and water is known to be from the side of Chesed. And there is a purity from the side of the left, as it is written (Numbers 31:23), "every thing that may abide the fire, you shall make it go through the fire, and it shall be pure."

And so vessels are purified in two ways: with water, namely immersion for eating vessels that have not been used with fire, or purification by fire if they were used with fire - as Scripture says, "every thing that may abide the fire, you shall make it go through the fire, and it shall be pure," and so on, "whatever may not abide the fire you shall make go through the water."

And so too concerning the purification of souls from their blemish - according to the blemish is the purification required - namely, the four categories of atonement that Rabbi Yishmael would expound (Yoma 86a): if a person transgressed a positive commandment and repented, he is forgiven at once, as it is said (Jeremiah 3:22), "return, backsliding children, I will heal your backslidings." This category of atonement is from the side of Chesed, for it is known (Tikkunei Zohar 107b) that the 248 positive commandments are from the side of the right, and the negative commandments from the side of the left - and therefore, the blemish of a positive commandment, which is in Chesed, once he has repented, he is forgiven at once, meaning that the purification from the waters of Chesed purifies him, and he is forgiven at once.

And the transgression of a positive commandment is when he is lazy in fulfilling the commandments - such as matzah on Passover and the like - namely, nullifying a commandment by sitting and not acting. And its remedy is alacrity from now on to fulfill what is within his power, and the water, namely the waters of the supernal atonement, will flow and wash away that blemish in the soul - for even nullifying a commandment causes a blemish in the soul, though not as great as transgressing a negative commandment - and purification in the waters of the mikveh will avail to purify what he was lazy about in the commandment. And the reason is that when a person fulfills the commandment, he draws supernal light to clothe his soul, but when he nullifies the commandment, immediately the external force is present there and rests upon him - for they are called "these" [eleh, associated with idolatry] and rest in any place empty of holiness, as explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (page 128a), that they rest upon a person for free, and especially when he is idle, "like finds like" and is aroused. And therefore, in order to strip that spirit of impurity from himself, purification in the waters of the mikveh, which are from the side of Chesed, is needed.

And when the blemish is in a negative commandment - namely the second category of atonement: if a person transgressed a negative commandment and repents, repentance suspends [punishment] and the Day of Atonement atones, as it is said (Leviticus 16:30), "for on this day He shall atone for you, to purify you." If a person transgressed [a sin punishable by] karet or death by the court and repents, repentance and the Day of Atonement suspend, and suffering finishes the atonement, as it is said (Psalms 89:33), "then I will visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with plagues." But one who has profaned the Name, and so on [is different]. Behold, these three categories are all, in general, negative commandments, and therefore their purification is all through the fire of Gevurah - for the fast of the Day of Atonement purifies through the affliction of the soul and the offering of one's fat and blood, melted in the fire of the affliction, as will be further explained concerning fasting: that fasting is a purifying fire against the fire of the evil inclination, along the lines of "every thing that may abide the fire"; and so suffering and plagues are all certainly purification from the side of fire - and needless to say the day of death. And the nature of fire is to refine both inside and out - along the lines of the blemish that boiled itself in the fire of the evil inclination, so purification and refinement are needed - and therefore the essence of purification is through fire, along the lines of (Pesachim, chapter 2, mishnah 1), "there is no removal of chametz except by burning." And therefore fasting is efficacious for a penitent to purify and refine him inside and out, and likewise the wearing of sackcloth on his flesh.

And in the Torah both of these purifications are found, and therefore our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained that the Torah is likened to fire, as it is said (Jeremiah 23:29), "is not My word like fire," and is likened to water, as it is said (Isaiah 55:1), "ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters" - and the reason is that the Torah is the secret of the middle line, so it is fitting that everything be included within it.

And all the particular aspects explained are all found in the Torah - whether to strip the spirit of impurity, or to cool the impurity from the fire of the evil inclination, or to refine the evil inclination - and therefore it is written of it (Psalms 12:7), "the words of the LORD are pure words."

And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Parashat Kedoshim, page 80b), that the essence of purification is through Torah, in these words: come and see, a person is never purified except through the words of Torah - therefore words of Torah do not receive impurity, because it stands to purify these impure ones, and healing is found in the Torah, as it is written (Proverbs 3:8), "it shall be healing to your navel, and marrow to your bones," and it is written (ibid. 10:27), "the fear of the LORD adds days." Purity is found in the Torah, as it is written (Psalms 19:10), "the fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever" - what is "enduring forever"? That it stands constantly in that purity and never departs from it - to this point.

And the essence of the purification of thought is through the occupation with Torah, as they said, of blessed memory (Kiddushin 30b): I created the evil inclination, I created for it the Torah as its antidote. And Maimonides wrote at the end of the Laws of Forbidden Relations, in these words: more than all this, they said, one should turn himself and his thought to words of Torah and broaden his mind with wisdom, for thoughts of forbidden relations gain strength only in a heart empty of wisdom - and concerning wisdom it says (Proverbs 5:19), "a loving hind and a graceful doe," and so on. And therefore we placed, in the matter of purity, the purity of Torah last, because it rises above all and is the essence of all purifications: "purity brings one to holiness."
